summary: Peri Bhaskararao (1947–2021) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor of Phonetics and Phonology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1976–1996) and held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1996–2011).

Peri Sarveswara Sharma (1926–2000) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Wilhelm Rau from around 1967 to 1971. He later taught Ryutaro Tsuchida and held a post at the University of Marburg from 1971 to 1991.

Perry Link (born 1944) is a sinologist who completed his B.A. at Harvard University (~1962–1966). His academic career includes posts at Princeton University (1973–1977), UCLA (1977–1988), and UC Riverside (~2008).

Perry Schmidt-Leukel (born 1954) specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, completing his degrees and Habilitation at the University of Munich. He held posts at Munich, Innsbruck, Salzburg, Glasgow (2000–2009), and Münster (2009–2023).

Peter Adamson (born 1972) works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Williams College (~1990–1994) and the University of Notre Dame (~1995–2001), later holding posts at King's College London (~2000–2012) and the University of Munich (~2012).

Peter Alan Roberts is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche in 1979, and completed his doctoral studies under supervisors Michael Aris and Richard Gombrich.

Peter C. Bisschop (born 1972) is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Groningen in 2004 under Hans T. Bakker and Harunaga Isaacson. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, Edinburgh (2005–2010), and Leiden (attested 2011–2026).

Peter Connolly is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed his BA, MA, and Ph.D. at Lancaster University and served as a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Chichester in 1980.

Peter D. Hershock (born 1958) works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Educated at Yale University and under traditional teachers Ji Kwang Dae Poep Sa Nim and Seungsahn Haengwon, he held positions at the East-West Center and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.
Peter Ebbatson is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of Oxford under the doctoral supervision of Walpola Rahula.

Peter Fenner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche and advisers N. Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch. He held an academic post at Deakin University.

Peter Francis Kornicki (born 1950) specializes in Japanology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Oxford, Tokyo University of Education, and under Masamichi Asukai and Mitsukuni Yoshida, he held posts at Tasmania, Kyoto, and Cambridge (~1985–2014).

Peter Gaeffke (1927–2005) was an Indologist who completed his PhD at Mainz under Ernst Schwarz in 1952, also studying at Regensburg and DIAS. He held posts at Mainz, Utrecht (1964), and the University of Pennsylvania (1972; 1975–2003).

Peter Gyallay-Pap is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at the London School of Economics by 1990. He held an adjunct position at Adams State University, attested in 2007.

Peter Harvey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies who founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996. He held a post as Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland (attested 2000–2015).
Peter Haskel is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He pursued graduate studies at Columbia University, where he studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

Peter J. Wilson (1933–2005) earned his Ph.D. at Yale University (~1956–1961). Over his career, he taught at Yale (~1961–1963), Vassar College (~1963–1964), University of Washington (~1964–1971), Bennington College, and University of Otago (~1971–1998).

Peter James Gilks works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang, under several Geshes and Khensurs, and earned his PhD at the Australian National University (attested 2010) under doctoral supervisor John Powers.
Peter K. Austin (born 1952) is a linguist who studied at the Australian National University from 1975 to 1978. He later held an academic post at SOAS University of London from around 2002 to 2016.

Peter Koret is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London. He has held academic posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.
